nodes.name: Multiplicative function
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a number field. A \emph{multiplicative function} is a function $\chi\colon\mathbb{F}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ that satisfies $\chi(mn)=\chi(m)\chi(n)$ for all $m,n\in\mathbb{F}$. We denote the family of multiplicative functions of modulus 1 by $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{F}}$.
nodes.section: 1.1 Structure theory in the finite setting

nodes.name: Frantzikinakis-Host structure theorem for multiplicative functions on Z
nodes.statement: They showed that for any multiplicative function $\chi$ on $\mathbb{Z}$ and any $d\in\mathbb{N}$, one can decompose $\chi$ into the sum of two functions $\chi_{s}+\chi_{u}$ plus an error term such that $\chi_{s}$ is an ``approximately periodic" function and $\chi_{u}$ has small $U^{d}$-Gowers norm. Moreover, $\chi_{s}$ can be written as the convolution of $\chi$ and a well-behaved function.
nodes.section: 1.1 Structure theory in the finite setting
nodes.statement_short: Every bounded multiplicative function on Z splits into an approximately periodic part plus a part with small U^d norm plus error.
assumptions: any multiplicative function $\chi$ on $\mathbb{Z}$ and any $d\in\mathbb{N}$
conclusions: one can decompose $\chi$ into the sum of two functions $\chi_{s}+\chi_{u}$ plus an error term such that $\chi_{s}$ is an ``approximately periodic" function and $\chi_{u}$ has small $U^{d}$-Gowers norm
$\chi_{s}$ can be written as the convolution of $\chi$ and a well-behaved function

nodes.name: Structure theorem for multiplicative functions in general number fields
nodes.statement: Frantzikinakis and Host asked in ~\cite{FH} whether the structure theorem still holds for multiplicative functions in a general number field $\mathbb{F}$.

nodes.name: Partition regularity of three-variable polynomial equations
nodes.statement:
Specifically, we study the following question:
suppose $p(x,y,z)$ is a polynomial of 3 variables over some number field $\mathbb{F}$. For any finite coloring of $\mathbb{F}$, can we find distinct numbers $x,y,z\in\mathbb{F}$ of the same color such that $p(x,y,z)=0$?
nodes.section: 1.2 Partition regularity results for quadratic forms
nodes.statement_short: For a 3-variable polynomial p over a number field, does every finite colouring contain distinct monochromatic x,y,z with p(x,y,z)=0?

nodes.name: Rado's theorem
nodes.statement:
The case when the polynomial $p$ is linear and $\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{Z}$  was completely solved by Rado ~\cite{Rado}: for $a,b,c\in\mathbb{Z}$, the equation
$ax+by+cz=0$ is partition regular if and only if either $a+b, b+c, a+c$ or $a+b+c$ is 0 (the original result is stated for $\mathbb{N}$ but a similar result holds for $\mathbb{Z}$).
nodes.section: 1.2 Partition regularity results for quadratic forms
nodes.statement_short: ax+by+cz=0 is partition regular over Z iff one of a+b, b+c, a+c, a+b+c vanishes.
conclusions:
the equation
$ax+by+cz=0$ is partition regular if and only if either $a+b, b+c, a+c$ or $a+b+c$ is 0

nodes.name: Partition regularity
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a number field, or a subset of some number field. An equation $p(x,y,n)\colon \mathbb{F}^{3}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ is \emph{partition regular} in $\mathbb{F}$ if for any partition of $\mathbb{F}$ into finitely many disjoint sets, for some $n\in \mathbb{F}$, one of the cells contains distinct $x$ and $y$ that satisfy $p(x,y,n)=0$.
nodes.section: 1.2 Partition regularity results for quadratic forms
nodes.statement_short: An equation p(x,y,n) is partition regular in F if every finite partition has a cell with distinct x,y solving p(x,y,n)=0 for some free n.

nodes.name: Furstenberg-Sarkozy theorem
nodes.statement: It is a classical result of Furstenberg ~\cite{7} and Sark\"{o}zy ~\cite{25} that the equation $x-y=n^{2}$ is partition regular in $\mathbb{N}$.
nodes.section: 1.2 Partition regularity results for quadratic forms
conclusions: the equation $x-y=n^{2}$ is partition regular in $\mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Khalfalah-Szemeredi theorem
nodes.statement: A result of Khalfalah and Szemer\'{e}di ~\cite{KS} is that the equation $x+y=n^{2}$ is partition regular in $\mathbb{N}$.
nodes.section: 1.2 Partition regularity results for quadratic forms
conclusions: the equation $x+y=n^{2}$ is partition regular in $\mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Frantzikinakis-Host partition regularity of ax^2+by^2=n^2
nodes.statement: For example, they proved that the equation $ax^{2}+by^{2}=n^{2}$ is partition regular in $\mathbb{N}$ if $a,b,a+b$ are non-zero square integers (for example, $a=16, b=9$).
nodes.section: 1.2 Partition regularity results for quadratic forms
conclusions: the equation $ax^{2}+by^{2}=n^{2}$ is partition regular in $\mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Partition regularity of x^2+y^2=n^2 and x^2-y^2=n^2 over N
nodes.statement: However, the partition regularity result in $\mathbb{N}$ for other quadratic equations, for example, $x^{2}+y^{2}=n^{2}$ or $x^{2}-y^{2}=n^{2}$, remains open.
nodes.section: 1.2 Partition regularity results for quadratic forms

nodes.name: Partition regularity transfers from N to Z[i]
nodes.statement: Since $\mathbb{N}$ is a subset of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, every polynomial equation which is partition regular in $\mathbb{N}$ will also be partition regular in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$.
nodes.section: 1.2 Partition regularity results for quadratic forms
conclusions: every polynomial equation which is partition regular in $\mathbb{N}$ will also be partition regular in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$

nodes.name: Partition regularity of x^2-y^2=n^2 over the Gaussian integers
nodes.statement: The equation $p(x,y,n)=x^{2}-y^{2}-n^{2}$ is partition regular in $\mathbb{Z}[i]\backslash \{0\}$. Equivalently, the system of equations \begin{equation} \nonumber \begin{split} & p_{1}((x_{1},x_{2}),(y_{1},y_{2}),(n_{1},n_{2}))=x_{1}^{2}-x_{2}^{2}-y_{1}^{2}+y_{2}^{2}-n_{1}^{2}+n_{2}^{2}; \\& p_{2}((x_{1},x_{2}),(y_{1},y_{2}),(n_{1},n_{2}))=x_{1}x_{2}-y_{1}y_{2}-n_{1}n_{2} \end{split} \end{equation} is partition regular in $\mathbb{Z}^{2}\backslash \{(0,0)\}$.
nodes.section: 1.2 Partition regularity results for quadratic forms
nodes.statement_short: x^2-y^2=n^2 is partition regular in Z[i]\{0}; equivalently a pair of quadratic equations is partition regular in Z^2\{0}.
conclusions: The equation $p(x,y,n)=x^{2}-y^{2}-n^{2}$ is partition regular in $\mathbb{Z}[i]\backslash \{0\}$

nodes.section: 2 Precise statement of the main theorems

nodes.name: Convention on Gaussian integers and the prime N-tilde
nodes.statement: Whenever we write an element in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ in the form $a+bi$, we always assume without explicitly writing this that $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$. Throughout, we assume that an integer $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ is given: its precise value depends on the applications we have in mind. We consider $\ell$ as fixed and the dependence on $\ell$ is always left implicit. For $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\tilde{N}$ be the smallest prime number (in $\mathbb{N}$) greater than $100\ell N$. Therefore, by Bertrand's postulate, $\tilde{N}\leq 200\ell N$. Throughout this paper, we always assume $\tilde{N}$ is the integer dependent on $N$ defined as above. For any function $f\colon R_{\tilde{N}}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$, we use the convention that $f(a+bi)=f((a+\tilde{N})+bi)=f(a+(b+\tilde{N})i)$, meaning that the addition is taken mod $R_{\tilde{N}}$.
nodes.section: 2 Precise statement of the main theorems
nodes.statement_short: Fix l; N-tilde is the smallest prime above 100 l N (so at most 200 l N); functions on R_{N-tilde} are taken periodically mod N-tilde.
nodes.label: conv

nodes.name: Multiplication by gamma is a bijection of R_N-tilde
nodes.statement: The reason that we work on the set $R_{\tilde{N}}$ rather than $R_{N}$ is that if $\vert\gamma\vert^{2}<\tilde{N}$, the map $\beta\to\gamma\beta$ is a bijection from $R_{\tilde{N}}$ to itself (see also the discussion after Proposition \ref{c4} for the reason).
nodes.section: 2 Precise statement of the main theorems

nodes.name: Convolution product
nodes.statement: The convolution product of two functions $f,g\colon R_{\tilde{N}}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ is defined by \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} f*g(\alpha)=\mathbb{E}_{\beta\in R_{\tilde{N}}}f(\alpha-\beta)g(\beta), \end{split} \end{equation} where for any function $f\colon S\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ on a finite set $S$, we denote $\mathbb{E}_{x\in S}f(x)=\frac{1}{\vert S\vert}\sum_{x\in S}f(x)$. Here $\vert S\vert$ denotes the cardinality of $S$.
nodes.section: 2 Precise statement of the main theorems

nodes.name: Fourier transformation on R_N-tilde
nodes.statement: For any $\alpha=\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}i,\beta=\beta_{1}+\beta_{2}i\in R_{\tilde{N}}$, write \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} \alpha\circ_{N}\beta=\frac{1}{\tilde{N}}(\alpha_{1}\beta_{1}+\alpha_{2}\beta_{2}). \end{split} \end{equation} For any function $f\colon R_{\tilde{N}}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ and $\bold{\xi}=\xi_{1}+\xi_{2}i\in R_{\tilde{N}}$, we let $\widehat{f}\colon R_{\tilde{N}}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ denote the \emph{Fourier transformation} of $f$ \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} \widehat{f}(\bold{\xi})=\mathbb{E}_{\alpha\in R_{\tilde{N}}}f(\alpha)e(-\alpha\circ_{N}\bold{\xi}) \end{split} \end{equation} for all $\bold{\xi}\in R_{\tilde{N}}$, where $e(x)=\exp(2\pi ix)$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.section: 2 Precise statement of the main theorems

nodes.name: Gowers uniformity norms
nodes.statement: For $d\geq 1$, we define the \emph{$d$-th Gowers uniformity norm} of $f$ on $R_{\tilde{N}}$ inductively by \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} \Vert f\Vert_{U^{1}(R_{\tilde{N}})}=\Bigl\vert\mathbb{E}_{\alpha\in R_{\tilde{N}}}f(\alpha)\Bigr\vert \end{split} \end{equation} and \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} \Vert f\Vert_{U^{d+1}(R_{\tilde{N}})}=\Bigl(\mathbb{E}_{\beta\in R_{\tilde{N}}}\Vert f_{\beta}\cdot\overline{f}\Vert_{_{U^{d}(R_{\tilde{N}})}}^{2^{d}}\Bigr)^{1/2^{d+1}} \end{split} \end{equation} for $d\geq 1$, where $\overline{f}$ denotes the conjugate of $f$ and $f_{\beta}(\alpha)=f(\beta+\alpha)$ for all $\alpha\in R_{\tilde{N}}$.
nodes.section: 2 Precise statement of the main theorems
nodes.statement_short: Inductive definition of the U^d Gowers norm on R_N-tilde via multiplicative derivatives f_beta * conj(f).

nodes.name: Partition regularity theorem for a special class of quadratic equations on Z[i]
nodes.statement: (Partition regularity theorem for a special class of equations on $\mathbb{Z}[i]$). Let $p$ be a quadratic equation of the form \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} p(x,y,n)=ax^{2}+by^{2}+cn^{2}+dxy+exn+fyn \end{split} \end{equation} for some $a,b,c,d,e,f\in\mathbb{Z}[i]$. If all of $\sqrt{e^{2}-4ac}, \sqrt{f^{2}-4bc},\sqrt{(e+f)^{2}-4c(a+b+d)}$ belong to $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, then $p(x,y,n)$ is partition regular in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$.
nodes.statement_short: A quadratic form p(x,y,n) over Z[i] whose three discriminant-type quantities are perfect squares in Z[i] is partition regular in Z[i].
conclusions: $p(x,y,n)$ is partition regular in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$

nodes.name: Multiplicative Folner sequence
nodes.statement: The sequence $\{\Phi_{N}\}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ of finite subsets of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ is a \emph{multiplicative F${\o}$lner sequence} if for every $\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}[i]$, \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\vert \alpha\Phi_{N}\triangle\Phi_{N}\vert}{\vert \Phi_{N}\vert}=0, \end{split} \end{equation} where $\alpha\Phi_{N}=\{\alpha x\colon x\in\Phi_{N}\}$.

nodes.name: Multiplicative density
nodes.statement: The \emph{multiplicative density} $d_{mult}(E)$ of a subset $E$ of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ (with respect to the multiplicative F${\o}$lner sequence $\{\Phi_{N}\}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$) is defined to be \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} d_{mult}(E)=\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\vert E\cap\Phi_{N}\vert}{\vert \Phi_{N}\vert}. \end{split} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Action by dilation
nodes.statement: An \emph{action by dilation} on a probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ is a family $\{T_{\alpha}\}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}[i]}$ of invertible measure preserving transformations of $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ that satisfy $T_{1}=id$ and $T_{\alpha}\cdot T_{\beta}=T_{\alpha\beta}$ for all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{Z}[i]$. Note that this can be extended to a measure preserving action $\{T_{z}\}_{z\in\mathbb{Q}[i]}$ by defining $T_{\alpha/\beta}=T_{\alpha}T_{\beta}^{-1}$ for all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{Z}[i], \beta\neq 0$, where $\mathbb{Q}[i]$ is the set of Gaussian rational numbers.
nodes.genus: family $\{T_{\alpha}\}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}[i]}$ of invertible measure preserving transformations

nodes.name: Furstenberg correspondence principle
nodes.statement: (Furstenberg correspondence principle). Let $E$ be a subset of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$. Then there exist an action by dilation $\{T_{\alpha}\}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}[i]}$ on a probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ and a set $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)=d_{mult}(E)$ such that for all $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and for all $\alpha_{1},\dots,\alpha_{k}\in\mathbb{Z}[i]$, we have \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} d_{mult}(\alpha_{1}^{-1}E\cap\dots\cap \alpha_{k}^{-1}E)\geq\mu(T_{\alpha_{1}}^{-1}A\cap\dots\cap T_{\alpha_{k}}^{-1}A), \end{split} \end{equation} where $\alpha^{-1}E=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}[i]\colon \alpha x\in E\}$.
nodes.statement_short: A set E in Z[i] of positive multiplicative density is modelled by a set A in a dilation system, with intersection densities bounded below by measures.

Let $\{T_{\alpha}\}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}[i]}$ be an action by dilation on a probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$. Then for every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exist $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{Z}[i]$ such that $(\alpha+\gamma_{1}\beta)(\alpha+\gamma_{2}\beta)$ and $(\alpha+\gamma_{3}\beta)(\alpha+\gamma_{4}\beta)$ are distinct and non-zero, and \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} \mu(T_{(\alpha+\gamma_{1}\beta)(\alpha+\gamma_{2}\beta)}^{-1}A\cap T_{(\alpha+\gamma_{3}\beta)(\alpha+\gamma_{4}\beta)}^{-1}A)>0. \end{split} \end{equation} Moreover, if $\gamma_{1},\gamma_{2},\gamma_{3},\gamma_{4}$ are pairwise distinct, we have that \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}_{(\alpha,\beta)\in\Theta_{N}}\mu(T_{(\alpha+\gamma_{1}\beta)(\alpha+\gamma_{2}\beta)}^{-1}A\cap T_{(\alpha+\gamma_{3}\beta)(\alpha+\gamma_{4}\beta)}^{-1}A)>0, \end{split} \end{equation} where $\Theta_{N}=\{(\alpha,\beta)\in R_{N}\times R_{N}\colon \alpha+\gamma_{i}\beta\in R_{N}, i=1,2,3\}$.

nodes.name: Classification of Gaussian primes
nodes.statement: The prime elements $p$ of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, up to a multiple of unit elements, is of one of the following three forms: (i) $p=1+i$; (ii) $p=a+bi, a^{2}+b^{2}=p_{0}, p_{0}\equiv 1 \mod 4$; (iii) $p=p_{0}, p_{0}\equiv 3 \mod 4$. Here $p_{0}$ is a prime in $\mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.name: Gaussian primes of equal norm
nodes.statement: Let $p=p_{1}+p_{2}i, q=q_{1}+q_{2}i\in\mathbb{P}[i]$. If $\mathcal{N}(p)=\mathcal{N}(q)$, then either (i) $p$ and $q$ conjugate with each other; or (ii) $\vert p_{1}\vert=\vert q_{1}\vert, \vert p_{2}\vert=\vert q_{2}\vert$. In particular, for any $p\in\mathbb{P}[i]$, the cardinality of the set $\mathcal{D}_{p}\coloneqq\{q\in\mathbb{P}[i]\colon \mathcal{N}(p)=\mathcal{N}(q)\}$ is at most 4.
nodes.statement_short: Two Gaussian primes of equal norm are conjugate or agree in absolute coordinates, so at most 4 primes share a norm.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.5
nodes.statement: Since the norm of the three types of primes in Theorem \ref{cls} are different, $\mathcal{N}(p)=\mathcal{N}(q)$ implies that $p$ and $q$ are of the same type. If they are of type (i) or (iii), then we are done, and $\vert\mathcal{D}_{p}\vert\leq 4$. If they are of type (ii), then $p_{1}^{2}+p_{2}^{2}=q_{1}^{2}+q_{2}^{2}=p_{0}$ for some prime $p_{0}\equiv 1 \mod 4$. Let $A=p_{1}+q_{1}, B=p_{1}-q_{1}, C=p_{2}+q_{2}, D=p_{2}-q_{2}$, then $AB=CD$. If one of $A,B,C,D$ is 0, then we are done. If $ABCD\neq 0$, let $a>0$ be the greatest common divisor of $A$ and $C$ and suppose $A=ab, C=ac$ for some $b,c\in\mathbb{Z}$. Thus $bB=cD$ and $b|D, c|B$. Assume that $B=d'c, D=bd$. Then $AB=CD$ implies $d=d'$. So $p_{0}=p_{1}^{2}+p_{2}^{2}=(\frac{A+B}{2})^{2}+(\frac{C-D}{2})^{2}=(\frac{ab+cd}{2})^{2}+(\frac{ac-bd}{2})^{2}=\frac{(a^{2}+d^{2})(b^{2}+c^{2})}{4}$. Since $p_{0}$ is a prime, one of $a^{2}+d^{2}, b^{2}+c^{2}$ equals to either 1,2, or 4. Since $ABCD\neq 0$, one of $a^{2}+d^{2}, b^{2}+d^{2}$ must equal to 2. Suppose $a^{2}+d^{2}=2$. Then $a,d=\pm 1$. So $A=\pm D, B=\pm C$. In any case, we have $\vert p_{1}\vert=\vert q_{1}\vert, \vert p_{2}\vert=\vert q_{2}\vert$, and $\vert\mathcal{D}_{p}\vert\leq 4$.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on the type of the primes; for type (ii) factor AB=CD and use primality of p_0.

nodes.name: Katai's Lemma
nodes.statement: (Katai's Lemma). For every $\epsilon>0$ and $K_{0}\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist $\delta=\delta(\epsilon,K_{0})>0$ and $K=K(\epsilon,K_{0})>K_{0}$ such that the following holds: If $N$ is sufficiently large with respect to $K$ and $f\colon R_{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ is a function with $\vert f\vert\leq 1$, and \begin{equation} \begin{split} \max_{p,q\in\mathbb{P}[i], K_{0}<\mathcal{N}(p)<\mathcal{N}(q)<K}\frac{1}{\vert R_{N}\vert}\Bigl\vert\sum_{\alpha\in R_{N}/p\cap R_{N}/q}f(p\alpha)\overline{f}(q\alpha)\Bigr\vert<\delta, \end{split} \end{equation} then \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} \sup_{\chi\in\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{Z}[i]}}\Bigl\vert\mathbb{E}_{\alpha\in R_{N}}\chi(\alpha)f(\alpha)\Bigr\vert<\epsilon, \end{split} \end{equation} where $R_{N}/p=\{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}[i]\colon p\alpha\in R_{N}\}$.
nodes.statement_short: If f has small correlations between its dilates by distinct small Gaussian primes p,q, then f is asymptotically orthogonal to all multiplicative functions.

nodes.name: U^2 decomposition theorem
nodes.statement: ($U^{2}$ decomposition theorem). For every $\epsilon>0$, there exist positive integers $Q=Q(\epsilon),R=R(\epsilon),N_{0}=N_{0}(\epsilon)$ such that for $N\geq N_{0}$, there exists a kernel $\phi_{N,\epsilon}$ on $R_{\tilde{N}}$ with the following property: For every $\chi\in\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{Z}[i]}$, writing $\chi_{N,s}=\chi_{N}*\phi_{N,\epsilon}$ and $\chi_{N,u}=\chi_{N}-\chi_{N,s}$, we have (i)$\vert\chi_{N,s}(\alpha+Q)-\chi_{N,s}(\alpha)\vert, \vert\chi_{N,s}(\alpha+Qi)-\chi_{N,s}(\alpha)\vert\leq\frac{R}{N}$ for every $\alpha\in R_{\tilde{N}}$; (ii)$\Vert\chi_{N,u}\Vert_{U^{2}(R_{\tilde{N}})}\leq\epsilon$. Moreover, for every $N\in\mathbb{N}, \bold{\xi}\in R_{\tilde{N}}$ and $0<\epsilon'\leq\epsilon$, we have $\widehat{\phi_{N,\epsilon'}}(\bold{\xi})\geq\widehat{\phi_{N,\epsilon}}(\bold{\xi})\geq 0$.

nodes.statement: We show that $\phi_{N,\epsilon}$ defined in (\ref{phi}) satisfies all the requirements. Suppose $0<\epsilon'\leq\epsilon$. Since $Q(\epsilon')\geq Q(\epsilon), V(\epsilon')\geq V(\epsilon)$ and $Q(\epsilon')$ is a multiple of $Q(\epsilon)$, we have $\Xi_{N,\epsilon}\subset\Xi_{N,\epsilon'}$ and $\widehat{\phi_{N,\epsilon'}}(\bold{\xi})\geq\widehat{\phi_{N,\epsilon}}(\bold{\xi})$ for every $\bold{\xi}\in R_{\tilde{N}}$. For every $\chi\in\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{Z}[i]},\bold{\xi}=\xi_{1}+\xi_{2}i\in R_{\tilde{N}}$, if $\vert\widehat{\chi_{N}}(\bold{\xi})\vert\geq\epsilon^{2}$, then by the definition of $Q, \Vert\frac{Q\xi_{i}}{\tilde{N}}\Vert\leq QV/\tilde{N}, i=1,2$. Then $\widehat{\phi_{N,\epsilon}}(\bold{\xi})\geq(1-\epsilon^{4}/2)^{2}\geq 1-\epsilon^{4}$. So $\vert\widehat{\chi_{N}}(\bold{\xi})-\widehat{\phi_{N,\epsilon}*\chi_{N}}(\bold{\xi})\vert\leq\epsilon^{4}\leq\epsilon^{2}$. The same estimate also holds if $\vert\widehat{\chi_{N}}(\bold{\xi})\vert\leq\epsilon^{2}$. Thus by identity (\ref{F}), we have \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} &\qquad \Vert\chi_{N,u}\Vert_{U^{2}(R_{\tilde{N}})}^{4}=\sum_{\bold{\xi}\in R_{\tilde{N}}}\vert\widehat{\chi_{N}}(\bold{\xi})-\widehat{\phi_{N,\epsilon}*\chi_{N}}(\bold{\xi})\vert^{4}\leq\epsilon^{4}\sum_{\bold{\xi}\in R_{\tilde{N}}}\vert\widehat{\chi_{N}}(\bold{\xi})-\widehat{\phi_{N,\epsilon}*\chi_{N}}(\bold{\xi})\vert^{2} \\&\leq\sum_{\bold{\xi}\in R_{\tilde{N}}}\vert\widehat{\chi_{N}}(\bold{\xi})\vert^{2}\leq\epsilon^{4}, \end{split} \end{equation} where the last estimate follows from Parseval's identity. This proves (ii). Lastly, using Fourier inversion formula and the estimate $\vert e(x)-1\vert\leq 2\pi\Vert x\Vert$, we get \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} &\vert\chi_{N,s}(\alpha+Q)-\chi_{N,s}(\alpha)\vert\leq\sum_{\bold{\xi}=\xi_{1}+\xi_{2}i\in R_{\tilde{N}}}\vert\widehat{\phi_{N,\epsilon}}(\bold{\xi})\vert\cdot 2\pi\Bigl\Vert\frac{Q\xi_{1}}{\tilde{N}}\Bigr\Vert \leq\vert\Xi_{N,\epsilon}\vert\cdot\frac{4\pi QV\lceil\epsilon^{-4}\rceil}{\tilde{N}}; \\& \vert\chi_{N,s}(\alpha+Qi)-\chi_{N,s}(\alpha)\vert\leq\sum_{\bold{\xi}=\xi_{1}+\xi_{2}i\in R_{\tilde{N}}}\vert\widehat{\phi_{N,\epsilon}}(\bold{\xi})\vert\cdot 2\pi\Bigl\Vert\frac{Q\xi_{2}}{\tilde{N}}\Bigr\Vert \leq\vert\Xi_{N,\epsilon}\vert\cdot\frac{ 4\pi QV\lceil\epsilon^{-4}\rceil}{\tilde{N}}. \end{split} \end{equation} Since $\vert\Xi_{N,\epsilon}\vert$ depends only on $\epsilon$, the theorem follows by taking $R=\vert\Xi_{N,\epsilon}\vert\cdot 4\pi QV\lceil\epsilon^{-4}\rceil$.
nodes.statement_short: Take the kernel phi_{N,eps}: monotone spectra give the moreover part, Parseval and identity (1) bound the U^2 norm of chi_N - chi_N*phi, and Fourier inversion gives approximate periodicity.

nodes.name: Filtration
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a connected, simply connected Lie group with identity element $e_{G}$ and let $d\in\mathbb{N}$. A \emph{filtration} on $G$ is a finite sequence $G_{\bullet}=\{G_{i}\}_{i=0}^{d+1}$ of closed connected subgroups of $G$ such that \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} G=G_{0}=G_{1}\supseteq G_{2}\supseteq\cdots\supseteq G_{d+1}=\{e_{G}\} \end{split} \end{equation} and $[G_{i},G_{j}]\subseteq G_{i+j}$ for all $i,j\geq 0$, where $[H,H']\coloneqq \{hh'h^{-1}h'^{-1}\colon h\in H, h'\in H'\}$ for all $H,H'<G$. The integer $d$ is called the \emph{order} of $G_{\bullet}$.
nodes.genus: finite sequence $G_{\bullet}=\{G_{i}\}_{i=0}^{d+1}$ of closed connected subgroups of $G$
nodes.label: filt

nodes.name: Filtration groups need not be commutator subgroups
nodes.statement: It is worth noting that $G_{i}$ is not necessarily the $i$-th commutator subgroup of $G$.

nodes.name: Nilmanifold of order 2
nodes.statement: Let $X=G/\Gamma$ be a nilmanifold of order 2 with filtration $G_{\bullet}$, i.e. $G$ is a Lie group with $[G,G]\subset G_{2},[G,G_{2}]=\{e_{G}\}$, and $\Gamma$ is a discrete cocompact subgroup of $G$.

nodes.name: Base point e_X
nodes.statement: The nilmanifold $X$ is endowed with a base point $e_{X}$ which is the projection to $X$ of the unit element of $G$.

nodes.name: Haar measure
nodes.statement: The \emph{Haar measure} $m_{X}$ of $X$ is the unique probability measure on $X$ that is invariant under this action.

nodes.name: Dimensions m, r, s
nodes.statement: We denote the dimension of $G$ by $m$ and the dimension of $G_{2}$ by $r$ and set $s=m-r$.

nodes.name: Mal'cev basis
Mal'cev homeomorphism
nodes.statement: We call $\phi$ the \emph{Mal'cev homeomorphism} of $G$ (or $X$) and call $\mathbb{R}^{m}$ the \emph{domain} of $\phi$.

nodes.name: Induced Mal'cev homeomorphism
nodes.statement: Any submanifold $Y$ of $X$ can be realized as $Y=\phi(V)$ for some subspace $V$ of $\mathbb{R}^{m}$. Then $\phi|_{Y}$ naturally induces a Mal'cev homeomorphism of $Y$. We call this induced map \emph{induced Mal'cev homeomorphism} from $X$ to $Y$.

nodes.name: Metric d_G
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be endowed with the Euclidean structure making $\mathcal{X}$ an orthonormal basis. This induces a Riemannian structure on $G$ that is invariant under right translations. The group $G$ is endowed with the associated geodesic distance, which we denote by $d_{G}$.

nodes.name: Quotient metric d_X
Continuity property
nodes.statement: (Continuity property). For every bounded subset $F$ of $G$, there exists $H>0$ such that (i) $d_{G}(g\cdot h,g\cdot h')\leq Hd_{G}(h,h')$ and $d_{X}(g\cdot x,g\cdot x')\leq Hd_{X}(x,x')$ for all $h,h'\in G, x,x'\in X$ and $g\in F$; (ii) for any $n\geq 1$, every $f\in\mathcal{C}^{n}(X)$ and every $g\in F$, writing $f_{g}(x)=f(g\cdot x)$, we have $\Vert f_{g}\Vert_{\mathcal{C}^{n}(X)}\leq H\Vert f\Vert_{\mathcal{C}^{n}(X)}$, where $\Vert \cdot\Vert_{\mathcal{C}^{n}(X)}$ is the usual $\mathcal{C}^{n}$-norm on $X$, and $\mathcal{C}^{n}(X)$ is the collection of functions with bounded $\mathcal{C}^{n}$-norm on $X$.
nodes.statement_short: Translations by a bounded set of group elements are uniformly Lipschitz and uniformly bounded on C^n norms.
conclusions: (i) $d_{G}(g\cdot h,g\cdot h')\leq Hd_{G}(h,h')$ and $d_{X}(g\cdot x,g\cdot x')\leq Hd_{X}(x,x')$ for all $h,h'\in G, x,x'\in X$ and $g\in F$;

(ii) for any $n\geq 1$, every $f\in\mathcal{C}^{n}(X)$ and every $g\in F$, writing $f_{g}(x)=f(g\cdot x)$, we have $\Vert f_{g}\Vert_{\mathcal{C}^{n}(X)}\leq H\Vert f\Vert_{\mathcal{C}^{n}(X)}$, where $\Vert \cdot\Vert_{\mathcal{C}^{n}(X)}$ is the usual $\mathcal{C}^{n}$-norm on $X$, and $\mathcal{C}^{n}(X)$ is the collection of functions with bounded $\mathcal{C}^{n}$-norm on $X$
nodes.label: cts

nodes.name: Vertical torus and nilcharacters
nodes.statement: We keep the same notations as above. The vertical torus is the sub-nilmanifold $G_{2}/(G_{2}\cap\Gamma)$. The basis induces an isometric identification between $G_{2}$ and $\mathbb{R}^{r}$, and thus of the vertical torus endowed with the quotient metric, with $\mathbb{T}^{r}$ endowed with its usual metric. Every $\bold{k}\in\mathbb{Z}^{r}$ induces a character $\bold{u}\rightarrow\bold{k}\cdot\bold{u}$ of the vertical torus. A function $F$ on $X$ is a \emph{nilcharacter with frequency $\bold{k}$} if $F(\bold{u}\cdot x)=e(\bold{k}\cdot\bold{u})F(x)$ for every $\bold{u}\in\mathbb{T}^{r}=G_{2}/(G_{2}\Gamma)$ and every $x\in X$. The nilcharacter is \emph{non-trivial} if its frequency is non-zero.

nodes.name: Maximal torus and horizontal characters
nodes.statement: Let $X=G/\Gamma$ be a nilmanifold of order 2 and let $m$ and $r$ be as above, and let $s=m-r$. The Mal'cev basis induces an isometric identification between the maximal torus $G/([G,G]\Gamma)$, endowed with the quotient metric, and $\mathbb{T}^{s}$, endowed with its usual metric. A \emph{horizontal character} is a continuous group homomorphism $\eta\colon G\rightarrow\mathbb{T}$ with trivial restriction to $\Gamma$.

nodes.name: Norm of a horizontal character
nodes.statement:
A horizontal character $\eta$
factors through the maximal torus, and we typically abuse notation
 and think of $\eta$ as a
character of the maximal torus, and identify $\eta$ with an element
 $\bold{k}$ of $\mathbb{Z}^{s}$ by the following
rule $\bold{\alpha}\rightarrow\bold{k}\cdot\bold{\alpha}=k_{1}\alpha_{1}+\dots+k_{s}\alpha_{s}$
for $\bold{\alpha}=(\alpha_{1},\dots,\alpha_{s})\in\mathbb{T}^{s}$ and
$\bold{k}=(k_{1},\dots,k_{s})\in\mathbb{Z}^{s}$.
We define $\Vert\eta\Vert\coloneqq\vert k_{1}\vert+\dots+\vert k_{s}\vert$.

nodes.name: Polynomial sequences
nodes.statement: Let $t\in\mathbb{N}$. For $\vec{n}=(n_{1},\dots,n_{t}),\vec{m}=(m_{1},\dots,m_{t})\in\mathbb{N}^{t}$, denote $\binom{\vec{n}}{\vec{m}}=\prod_{i=1}^{t}\binom{n_{i}}{m_{i}}$. For every $t$-tuple $\vec{n}=(n_{1},\dots,n_{t})\in\mathbb{Z}^{t}$, every group $G$ and every function $\phi\colon \mathbb{Z}^{t}\rightarrow G$, we denote $D_{\vec{n}}\phi\colon \mathbb{Z}^{t}\rightarrow G$ by $D_{\vec{n}}\phi(\vec{x})=\phi(\vec{x}+\vec{n})\phi^{-1}(\vec{x})$. A function $\phi\colon \mathbb{Z}^{t}\rightarrow G$ is called a \emph{polynomial sequence} (or a \emph{polynomial map}) of degree $d$ with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}=\{G_{i}\}_{i=0}^{d+1}$ if $D_{\vec{h_{j}}}\dots D_{\vec{h_{1}}}\phi\in G_{j}$ for any $1\leq j\leq d+1$ and any $\vec{h_{1}},\dots,\vec{h_{j}}\in\mathbb{Z}^{t}$.

nodes.name: Explicit form of degree 2 polynomial maps
nodes.statement: (Corollary of Lemma 6.7 in ~\cite{GT}). A map $\phi\colon\mathbb{Z}^{2}\rightarrow G$ is polynomial of degree 2 with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$ of order 2 if and only if it can be written as $\phi(m,n)=g_{0}g_{1,1}^{m}g_{1,2}^{n}g_{2,1}^{\binom{m}{2}}g_{2,2}^{mn}g_{2,3}^{\binom{n}{2}}$, where $g_{0},g_{1,1},g_{1,2}\in G, g_{2,1},g_{2,2},g_{2,3}\in G_{2}$.
conclusions: A map $\phi\colon\mathbb{Z}^{2}\rightarrow G$ is polynomial of degree 2 with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$ of order 2 if and only if it can be written as $\phi(m,n)=g_{0}g_{1,1}^{m}g_{1,2}^{n}g_{2,1}^{\binom{m}{2}}g_{2,2}^{mn}g_{2,3}^{\binom{n}{2}}$, where $g_{0},g_{1,1},g_{1,2}\in G, g_{2,1},g_{2,2},g_{2,3}\in G_{2}$
equivalent_conditions: A map $\phi\colon\mathbb{Z}^{2}\rightarrow G$ is polynomial of degree 2 with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$ of order 2
nodes.label: 2p

nodes.name: Interval [N]
nodes.statement: For every $N\in\mathbb{N}$, we write $[N]=\{1,\dots,N\}$.

nodes.name: The inverse theorem for Z^2 actions
nodes.statement: (The inverse theorem for $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$ actions). For every $\epsilon>0$, there exists $\delta=\delta(\epsilon)>0, N_{0}=N_{0}(\epsilon)\in\mathbb{N}$ and a nilmanifold $X=X(\epsilon)$ of order 2 with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$ such that for every $N\geq N_{0}$ and every $f\colon R_{\tilde{N}}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ with $\vert f\vert\leq 1$ and $\Vert f\Vert_{U^{3}(R_{\tilde{N}})}\geq\epsilon$, there exist a function $\Phi\colon X\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ with $\Vert\Phi\Vert_{Lip(X)}\leq 1$ and a polynomial sequence $g(m,n)\colon [\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]\rightarrow G$ of degree 2 on $G$ with respect to $G_{\bullet}$ such that $\vert\mathbb{E}_{m+ni\in R_{\tilde{N}}}f(m+ni)\Phi(g(m,n)\cdot e_{X})\vert\geq\delta$.
nodes.statement_short: A bounded function on R_N-tilde with large U^3 norm correlates with a degree 2 nilsequence on a fixed order-2 nilmanifold.
conclusions: there exist a function $\Phi\colon X\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ with $\Vert\Phi\Vert_{Lip(X)}\leq 1$ and a polynomial sequence $g(m,n)\colon [\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]\rightarrow G$ of degree 2 on $G$ with respect to $G_{\bullet}$ such that $\vert\mathbb{E}_{m+ni\in R_{\tilde{N}}}f(m+ni)\Phi(g(m,n)\cdot e_{X})\vert\geq\delta$
nodes.label: inv2

nodes.name: Modified U^3-inverse theorem
nodes.statement: (Modified $U^{3}$-inverse theorem). For every $\epsilon>0$, there exist $\delta=\delta(\epsilon)>0, M=M(\epsilon),N_{0}=N_{0}(\epsilon)\in\mathbb{N}$ and a finite family $\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}(\epsilon)$ of nilmanifolds of order 2, of dimension at most $M$ and having a vertical torus of dimension 1, such that: for every $N\geq N_{0}$, if $f\colon R_{\tilde{N}}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ is a function with $\vert f\vert\leq 1$ and $\Vert f\Vert_{U^{3}(R_{\tilde{N}})}\geq\epsilon$, then either (i) $\Vert f\Vert_{U^{2}(R_{\tilde{N}})}\geq\delta$; or (ii) there exists a nilmanifold $X$ belonging to the family $\mathcal{H}$, a polynomial map $g\colon\mathbb{Z}^{2}\rightarrow G$ of degree 2 with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$, and a nilcharacter $\bold{\psi}$ of $X$ with frequency 1, such that $\Vert\bold{\psi}\Vert_{\mathcal{C}^{2m}(X)}\leq 1$ and $\Bigl\vert\mathbb{E}_{m+ni\in R_{\tilde{N}}}f(m+ni)\bold{\psi}(g(m,n)\cdot e_{X})\Bigr\vert\geq\delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Large U^3 norm implies large U^2 norm or correlation with a frequency-1 nilcharacter along a degree 2 polynomial on a nilmanifold with 1-dimensional vertical torus.
assumptions: $f\colon R_{\tilde{N}}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ is a function with $\vert f\vert\leq 1$ and $\Vert f\Vert_{U^{3}(R_{\tilde{N}})}\geq\epsilon$
conclusions: (i) $\Vert f\Vert_{U^{2}(R_{\tilde{N}})}\geq\delta$

(ii) there exists a nilmanifold $X$ belonging to the family $\mathcal{H}$, a polynomial map $g\colon\mathbb{Z}^{2}\rightarrow G$ of degree 2 with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$, and a nilcharacter $\bold{\psi}$ of $X$ with frequency 1, such that $\Vert\bold{\psi}\Vert_{\mathcal{C}^{2m}(X)}\leq 1$ and $\Bigl\vert\mathbb{E}_{m+ni\in R_{\tilde{N}}}f(m+ni)\bold{\psi}(g(m,n)\cdot e_{X})\Bigr\vert\geq\delta$
nodes.label: mIU3

nodes.name: Box [N-vector]
nodes.statement: For any $t$-tuple $\vec{N}=(N_{1},\dots,N_{t})\in\mathbb{N}^{t}$, write $[\vec{N}]=[N_{1}]\times\dots\times[N_{t}]$.

nodes.name: Totally equidistributed sequences
nodes.statement: Let $X=G/\Gamma$ be a nilmanifold and $\vec{N}=(\tilde{N},\dots,N_{t})\in\mathbb{N}^{t}$ be a $t$-tuple. A sequence $g\colon[\vec{N}]\rightarrow G$ is called \emph{totally $\epsilon$-equidistributed} if \begin{equation} \begin{split} \Bigl\vert\mathbb{E}_{\vec{n}\in[\vec{N}]}\bold{1}_{P_{1}\times\dots\times P_{t}}(\vec{n})F(g(\vec{n})\cdot e_{X})\Bigr\vert\leq\epsilon \end{split} \end{equation} for all $F\in Lip(X)$ with $\Vert F\Vert_{Lip(X)}\leq 1$ and $\int F dm_{X}=0$ and all arithmetic progressions $P_{i}$ in $[N_{i}]$.
nodes.label: equid

nodes.name: Only t<=2 is used
nodes.statement: We only uses the case $t\leq 2$ and $N_{1}=N_{2}$ if $t=2$. But we state some of the definitions and results in full generality in case of further researches.

nodes.name: Smooth sequences
nodes.statement: Given a nilmanifold $G/\Gamma, M\in\mathbb{N}$, and $\vec{N}=(N_{1},\dots,N_{t})\in\mathbb{N}^{t}$, we say that the sequence $\epsilon\colon[\vec{N}]\rightarrow G$ is \emph{$(M,\vec{N})$-smooth} if for every $\vec{n}\in[\vec{N}]$, we have $d_{G}(\epsilon(\vec{n}),\bold{1}_{G})\leq M$ and $d_{G}(\epsilon(\vec{n}),\epsilon(\vec{n}-\vec{e_{i}}))\leq M/N_{i}$ for all $1\leq i\leq t$, where the $i$-th coordinate of $\vec{e_{i}}$ is 1 and all other coordinates are 0.

nodes.name: Rational elements and sequences
nodes.statement: We say an element $g\in G$ is \emph{$Q$-rational} for some $Q\in\mathbb{N}$ if there exists $m\leq Q$ such that $g^{m}\in\Gamma$. We say that $g$ is \emph{rational} if it is $Q$-rational for some $Q\in\mathbb{N}$. We say that a sequence $\gamma\colon[\vec{N}]\rightarrow G$ is \emph{$Q$-rational} if for every $\vec{n}\in[\vec{N}], \gamma(\vec{n})$ is $Q$-rational.

nodes.name: Rational subgroup
nodes.statement: A \emph{rational subgroup} $G'$ of $G$ is a closed and connected subgroup of $G$ such that its Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}'$ admits a base that has rational coordinates in the Mal'cev basis of $G$.

nodes.name: Induced filtration of subgroups
nodes.statement: Suppose $G$ is a group with filtration $G_{\bullet}=\{G_{i}\}_{i=0}^{d+1}$ and $G'$ is a subgroup of $G$. We denote $G'_{\bullet}=\{G_{i}\cap G\}_{i=0}^{d+1}$. This is a filtration of $G'$. We call $G'_{\bullet}$ the filtration induced by $G_{\bullet}$.

nodes.name: Factorization of polynomial sequences
nodes.statement: (Factorization of polynomial sequences, Theorem 10.2 in ~\cite{GT}). Suppose that $X=G/\Gamma$ is a nilmanifold of order 2 with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$. For every $M\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a finite collection $\mathcal{F}(M)$ of sub-nilmanifolds of $X$, each of the form $X'=G'/\Gamma'$, where $G'$ is a rational subgroup of $G$ and $\Gamma'=G'\cap\Gamma$, such that the following holds: For every function $\omega\colon\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{+}$ and every $M_{0}\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists $M_{1}=M_{1}(M_{0},X,\omega)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and every polynomial sequence of degree 2 $(g(m,n))_{(m,n)\in[\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]}$ in $G$ with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$, there exist $M\in\mathbb{N}$ with $M_{0}\leq M\leq M_{1}$, a nilmanifold $X'\in\mathcal{F}(M)$, and a decomposition \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} g(m,n)=\epsilon(m,n)g'(m,n)\gamma(m,n), (m,n)\in[\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}], \end{split} \end{equation} where $\epsilon,g',\gamma$ are polynomials of degree 2 with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$ such that (i) $\epsilon$ is $(M,(\tilde{N},\tilde{N}))$-smooth; (ii) $(g'(m,n))_{(m,n)\in[\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]}$ takes values in $G'$, and the finite sequence $(g'(m,n)\cdot e_{X'})_{(m,n)\in[\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]}$ is totally $\omega(M)$-equidistributed in $X'$ with the metric $d_{X'}$; (iii) $\gamma\colon[\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]\rightarrow G$ is $M$-rational, and $(\gamma(m,n)\cdot e_{X})_{(m,n)\in[\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]}$ is doubly periodic with periods at most $M$.
nodes.statement_short: Every degree 2 polynomial sequence factors as smooth times totally equidistributed on a rational sub-nilmanifold times periodic rational.
nodes.label: mFo

nodes.name: Modified factorization theorem
nodes.statement: (Modified factorization theorem). Let $X=G/\Gamma$ be a nilmanifold of order 2 with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$ and with vertical torus of dimension 1. For every $M\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a finite collection $\mathcal{F}(M)$ of sub-nilmanifolds of $X$, each of the form $X'=G'/\Gamma'$ with filtration $G'_{\bullet}$, where $G'$ is a rational subgroup of $G$ and $\Gamma'=G'\cap\Gamma$, and either (i) $G'$ is an abelian rational subgroup of $G$; or (ii) $G'$ is a non-abelian rational subgroup of $G$ and $G_{2}'/(G_{2}'\cap\Gamma')$ has dimension 1, such that the following holds: For every $\omega\colon\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{+}$ and every $M_{0}\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists $M_{1}=M_{1}(M_{0},X,\omega)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and every polynomial $g\colon\mathbb{Z}^{2}\rightarrow G$ of degree 2 with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$, there exist $M\in\mathbb{N}$ with $M_{0}\leq M\leq M_{1}$, a nilmanifold $X'\in\mathcal{F}(M)$, and a decomposition \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} g(m,n)=\epsilon(m,n)g'(m,n)\gamma(m,n), (m,n)\in[\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}] \end{split} \end{equation} such that (iii) $\epsilon$ is $(M,(\tilde{N},\tilde{N}))$-smooth; (iv) for any $(m,n)\in[\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]$, \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} g'(m,n)=g_{0}g_{1,1}^{m}g_{1,2}^{n}g_{2,1}^{\binom{m}{2}}g_{2,2}^{mn}g_{2,3}^{\binom{n}{2}}, \end{split} \end{equation} where $g_{0}, g_{1,1}, g_{1,2},g_{2,1},g_{2,2},g_{2,3}\in G'$, and moreover $g_{2,1},g_{2,2},g_{2,3}\in G'_{2}$ in case (ii), and $(g'(m,n)\cdot e_{X'})_{(m,n)\in[\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]}$ is totally $\omega(M)$-equidistributed in $X'$ with the metric $d_{X'}$; (v) $\gamma\colon[\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]\rightarrow G$ is $M$-rational, and $(\gamma(m,n))_{(m,n)\in[\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]}$ is doubly periodic with periods at most $M$.
nodes.statement_short: For order-2 nilmanifolds with 1-dim vertical torus, the equidistributed factor lies on an abelian sub-nilmanifold or one with 1-dim vertical torus, with explicit coefficients.
nodes.label: mF

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.17
nodes.statement: Let the integers $M_{1}, M$ and the nilmanifold $X'=G'/\Gamma'\in\mathcal{F} (M)$ be given by Theorem \ref{mFo}. Note that the sequence $(g(m,n))_{(m,n)\in[\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]}$ is a degree 2 polynomial sequence in $G$ with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$. Let $(g'(m,n))_{(m,n)\in[\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]}$ be the sequence given by the decomposition of Theorem \ref{mFo}. By Lemma \ref{2p}, we can write \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} g'(m,n)=g_{0}g_{1,1}^{m}g_{1,2}^{n}g_{2,1}^{\binom{m}{2}}g_{2,2}^{mn}g_{2,3}^{\binom{n}{2}} \end{split} \end{equation} for some $g_{0}, g_{1,1}, g_{1,2}\in G, g_{2,1},g_{2,2},g_{2,3}\in G_{2}$. It remains to show that $g_{0}, g_{1,1}, g_{1,2}\in G'$, $g_{2,1},g_{2,2},g_{2,3}\in G'_{2}$ for case (ii). Since $g_{0}=g(0,0)$, we have $g_{0}\in G'$. So the sequence $g''(m,n)=g_{0}^{-1}g'(m,n)$ also takes values in $G'$. Denote $$\partial_{(x,y)}g(m,n)=g(m+x,n+y)g(m,n)^{-1}.$$ Since $G$ is of order 2, $G_{2}$ is included in the center of $G$. Therefore, we obtain \begin{equation}\nonumber \begin{split} \partial_{(1,0)}g''(m,0)=g_{1,1}g_{2,1}^{m} \text{ and } \partial_{(1,0)}^{2}g''(m,0)=g_{2,1}. \end{split} \end{equation} It follows that $g_{1,1},g_{2,1}\in G'$. Similarly, $g_{1,2},g_{2,3}\in G'$. Thus the sequence $g'''(m,n)=g_{2,2}^{m,n}$ also takes values in $G'$, which implies $g_{2,2}\in G'$. If we are in case (i), then $G'$ is abelian and we are done. If $G'$ is not abelian, then $G'_{2}$ is a non-trivial subgroup of $G_{2}$. Moreover, $G'_{2}$ is closed and connected, and by hypothesis $G_{2}$ is isomorphic to the torus $\mathbb{T}$. It follows that $G'_{2}=G_{2}$. Hence $g_{2,1},g_{2,2},g_{2,3}\in G'_{2}$. This finishes the proof.

nodes.name: A variation of the quantitative Leibman Theorem
nodes.statement: (A variation of the quantitative Leibman Theorem). Let $X=G/\Gamma$ be a nilmanifold of order 2 and $t\in\mathbb{N}$. Since $\mathcal{N}(p)\neq \mathcal{N}(q)$, we have that $A+C\neq 0$. Thus
 \begin{equation}\nonumber
\begin{vmatrix}

A & B &  C\\

C & -B & A\\

-B & A-C & B\\

\end{vmatrix}=-(A+C)((A-C)^{2}+2B^{2})\neq 0,

nodes.name: Proof strategy for Proposition 7.9
nodes.statement:
Proposition \ref{est1} is the key difficulty of the paper, so we briefly explain the general strategy of the proof before we proceed. First of all, using the vertical Fourier transform, we may assume without loss of generality that $\Phi$ is a non-trivial nilcharacter. We may further simplify the argument to the case when $\beta=0$ and $g'$ does not have the constant term. 
By Lemma \ref{katai}, it suffices to study the total equidistribution property of the sequence $(g'(p\alpha),g'(q\alpha))_{\alpha\in R_{\tilde{N}}}$ on $G\times G$ with respect to the function $\Phi\otimes\overline{\Phi}$. This is studied carefully in Proposition \ref{last}, where we provide a necessary condition for the sequence $(g'(p\alpha),g'(q\alpha))_{\alpha\in R_{\tilde{N}}}$. Finally, this condition leads to a contradiction by a linear algebraic argument.

nodes.name: Overview of Proposition 7.25 and the Approximation Lemma
nodes.statement: It is worth making a few remarks about Proposition \ref{last}, which is the main technical part of the proof. Roughly speaking, we wish to give a necessary condition for a sequence $(g_{1}(\alpha),g_{2}(\alpha))_{\alpha\in R_{\tilde{N}}}$ on $G\times G$ of degree 2 not being totally equidistributed. If $(g_{1}(\alpha),g_{2}(\alpha))_{\alpha\in R_{\tilde{N}}}$ is not totally equidistributed, the Approximation Lemma (Lemma \ref{appro2}) allows us to replace any polynomial sequence on some sub-nilmanifold $H$ of $X\times X$ with another one lying on a sub-nilmanifold $H'$ of $H$ such that they have a similar total equidistribution behavior, unless $H$ satisfies some degeneracy property. This enables us to reduce the problem to the case where $(g_{1}(\alpha),g_{2}(\alpha))_{\alpha\in R_{\tilde{N}}}$ lies in a submanifold of $X\times X$ with additional algebriac structures, which leads to the necessary condition we desire.

$(I)$ $h_{j}(n)$ is not $S$-totally $\kappa_{j}$-equidistributed on $H_{j}$;

$(II)$ If $H_{j}$ is of type 1, then $h_{j}$ is a 2-polynomial;

$(III)$ If $j\geq 1$, then $H_{j}=H_{j-1}^{\underline{\bold{v}_{j}}}$ for some $\bold{v}_{j}$ non-trivial with respect of $H_{j-1}$ (recall Definition \ref{sg}) and of the same type as $H_{j-1}$. $(IV)$ The coefficients of the pair $(h_{j-1},h_{j})$ satisfy Property 2) of Lemma \ref{appro2} , for some function $D'_{j}$ and integer $w_{j}$ bounded by
some constant depending only on $X$ and $\kappa$.

nodes.name: Type 1: Leibman gives v_{i+1}; define H_{i+1} and continue or stop by its type
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Case that $H_{i}$ is of type 1.} By hypothesis $(II)$, $h_{i}$ is a 2-polynomial. Then
using Theorem \ref{Lei} on $H_{i}$,
there exist $D_{i+1}>0$ and a vector $\bold{v}_{i+1}\in\mathbb{Z}^{2s+2}$ non-trivial with respect to $V_{i}$ of the same type as $H_{i}$ with length no larger than $D_{i+1}$ such that
\begin{equation}\nonumber
    \begin{split}
     \Vert \bold{v}_{i+1}\cdot\tilde{\bold{c}_{i}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\leq\frac{D_{i+1}}{N}.
    \end{split}
  \end{equation}
  Let $H_{i+1}=H^{\underline{\bold{v}_{i+1}}}$ (recall Definition \ref{subgroup}). Then $V(H_{i+1})=V_{i+1}$ is of co-dimension $i+1$ since $\bold{v}_{i+1}$ is non-trivial with respect to $V_{i}$. Let
 $\Gamma_{i+1}=\Gamma_{0}\cap H_{i+1}, Y_{i+1}=H_{i+1}/\Gamma_{i+1}$.

 If $H_{i+1}$ is of type 1, then $(H_{i})_{2}=(H_{i+1})_{2}$. By Lemma \ref{appro2}, there exists
 a polynomial of the form $h_{i+1}(n)=v_{i+1}\Bigl(\bold{a}_{i+1}^{n}a_{i+1}'^{\binom{n}{2}},\bold{b}_{i+1}^{n}b_{i+1}'^{\binom{n}{2}}\Bigr)$
on $H_{i+1}$ ($a_{i+1}'(n),b_{i+1}'(n)\in G_{2}$) such that it is not $S$-totally $\kappa_{i+1}$-equidistributed on $H_{i+1}$ and the coefficients of the pair
$(h_{i},h_{i+1})$ satisfy Property 2) of Lemma \ref{appro2}
for some function $D'_{i+1}$ and integer $w_{i+1}$ bounded by some constant depending only on $X$ and $\kappa$. Thus $(IV)$ is
satisfied for the system $Y_{i+1}$ and the sequence $h_{i+1}$. By Property 1) of Lemma \ref{appro2}, $(I)$ is true since the pair $(H_{i},H_{i+1})$ is good by
 Lemma \ref{good}. $(II)$ also holds since $h_{i+1}$ is a 2-polynomial.

If $H_{i+1}$ is of type 2 and the pair $(H_{i},H_{i+1})$ is good, by Lemma \ref{appro2}, there exists
 a 3-polynomial $h_{i+1}(n)=v_{i+1}\Bigl(\bold{a}_{i+1}^{n}a_{i+1}'^{\binom{n}{2}}a_{i+1}''^{\binom{n}{3}},\bold{b}_{i+1}^{n}b_{i+1}'^{\binom{n}{2}}b_{i+1}''^{\binom{n}{3}}\Bigr)$
on $H_{i+1}$ ($a_{i+1}''(n),b_{i+1}''(n)\in G_{2}$) such that it is not $S$-totally $\kappa_{i+1}$-equidistributed on $H_{i+1}$ and the coefficients of the pair $(h_{i},h_{i+1})$ satisfy Property 2) of Lemma \ref{appro2}
for some function $D'_{i+1}$ and integer $w_{i+1}$ bounded by some constant depending only on $X$ and $\kappa$.  Thus $(IV)$ is
satisfied for the system $Y_{i+1}$ and the sequence $h_{i+1}$. $(I)$ is true by assumption. Condition $(II)$ is trivial since $H_{i+1}$ is of type 2.

If $H_{i+1}$ is of type 2 and the pair $(H_{i},H_{i+1})$ is not good, then we stop the induction procedure.

If $H_{i+1}$ is abelian, then we stop the induction procedure.

nodes.name: Type 2: same scheme, H_{i+1} is type 2 or abelian
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Case that $H_{i}$ is of type 2.} This time $h_{i}$ is a 3-polynomial and $H_{i}$ is $\bold{\lambda}$-shaped. Using Theorem \ref{Lei} on $H_{i}$,
there exist $D_{i+1}>0$ and a vector $\bold{v}_{i+1}\in\mathbb{Z}^{2s+2}$ non-trivial with respect to $V_{i}$ of the same type as $H_{i}$ with length no larger than $D_{i+1}$ such that
\begin{equation}\nonumber
    \begin{split}
     \Vert \bold{v}_{i+1}\cdot\tilde{\bold{c}_{i}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\leq\frac{D_{i+1}}{N}, \Vert \bold{v}_{i+1}\cdot \tilde{c'_{i}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\leq\frac{D_{i+1}}{N^{2}}.
    \end{split}
  \end{equation}
  Let $H_{i+1}=H^{\underline{V_{i+1}}}$. Then $V_{i+1}$ is of codimension $i+1$ since $\bold{v}_{i+1}$ is non-trivial with respect to $V_{i}$. Let
 $\Gamma_{i+1}=\Gamma_{0}\cap H_{i+1}, Y_{i+1}=H_{i+1}/\Gamma_{i+1}$.

 Since $H_{i}$ is of type 2, we have that $H_{i+1}$ is either of type 2 or abelian. If $H_{i+1}$ is of type 2, then $(H_{i})_{2}=(H_{i+1})_{2}$. By
 Lemma \ref{appro2}, there exists
 a 3-polynomial of the form $h_{i+1}(n)=v_{i+1}\Bigl(\bold{a}_{i+1}^{n}a_{i+1}'^{\binom{n}{2}}a_{i+1}''^{\binom{n}{3}},\bold{b}_{i+1}^{n}b_{i+1}'^{\binom{n}{2}}b_{i+1}''^{\binom{n}{3}}\Bigr)$
on $H_{i+1}$ ($a_{i+1}''(n),b_{i+1}''(n)\in G_{2}$)  such that it is not $S$-totally $\kappa_{i+1}$-equidistributed on $H_{i+1}$ and the coefficients of the pair
$(h_{i},h_{i+1})$ satisfy Property 2) of Lemma \ref{appro2}
for some function $D'_{i+1}$ and integer $w_{i+1}$ bounded by some constant depending only on $X$ and $\kappa$. Thus $(IV)$ is
satisfied for the system $Y_{i+1}$ and the sequence $h_{i+1}$. By Property 1) of Lemma \ref{appro2}, $(I)$ is true since the pair $(H_{i},H_{i+1})$ is good by
Lemma \ref{good}. Condition $(II)$ is trivial since $H_{i+1}$ is of type 2.

If $H_{i+1}$ is abelian, then we stop the induction procedure.

nodes.name: rank(A) < s: pull back a linear relation, conclusion (i)
nodes.statement:
First suppose that $rank(A)<s$. Since $\tilde{\bold{c}_{i+1}}=\tilde{(\bold{a}_{i+1},\bold{b}_{i+1})}=(\bold{t}A,\bold{t}A';\bold{t}\xi,\bold{t}\xi')$ for some $\bold{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{r}$, we deduce that there exist $F_{3}>0$ and $\bold{p}=(\bold{p}_{0},\bold{0})\in\mathbb{Z}^{s}\times\{0\}^{s+2}$ with $0<\Vert\bold{p}\Vert\leq F_{3}$ such that
$\Vert\bold{p}\cdot\tilde{\bold{c}_{i+1}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}=\Vert\bold{p}_{0}\cdot\widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\leq\frac{F_{3}}{N}$ (recall that
$\widehat{\bold{a}}$ is the first $s$ coordinates of $\bold{a}$ by Convention \ref{conv2}).
Since the coefficients of each pair $(h_{j},h_{j+1}) (0\leq j\leq i)$ satisfy Property 2) of Lemma \ref{appro2} and $\bold{p}$ is of type 1 (and thus is of the same type
as all subgroups of $H_{0}$), there exists $w\in\mathbb{Z}$ with $0<\vert w\vert\leq F_{4}$ such that
$\Vert w\bold{p}\cdot\tilde{\bold{c}_{0}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}=\Vert w\bold{p}_{0}\cdot\widehat{\bold{a}_{0}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\leq\frac{F_{4}}{N}$,
where $F_{4}=D'_{1}(F_{1}\cdot D'_{2}(\dots F_{1}\cdot D'_{i}(0)\dots))$. So the existence of $\eta_{1}$ in (i) is proved.
The existence of $\eta_{2}$ in (i) holds similarly and therefore conclusion (i) holds.

nodes.name: rank(A) = s forces B^G = 0, contradiction
nodes.statement: If $rank(A)= s$, by a simple computation using linear algebra, (\ref{ABA2}) implies that $B^{G}=0$. So $G$ is abelian, a contradiction.

nodes.statement_short: rank(A) = s forces B^G = 0, contradiction.

nodes.name: Terminal non-good pair: (1,1)-shaped H_{i+1} gives (i) or the matrix relation (ii)
nodes.statement:
If the pair $(H_{i},H_{i+1})$ is not good, by Lemma \ref{good}, we must have that $H_{i}$ is of type 1 and $H_{i+1}$ is of type 2,
and $H_{i+1}$ must be $(1,1)$-shaped. By a similar discussion,
we can still construct the system $Y_{i+1}$ and the sequence $h_{i+1}$ such that $(II),(III)$ and $(IV)$ hold (but $(I)$ may not hold).
Set $r=2s-i+1$. Since in this case $\bold{v}_{j}$ is of type 1 for all $0\leq j\leq i$, $H_{i+1}$ can be written as
\begin{equation}\nonumber
 \begin{split}
  H_{i+1}=\Bigl\{ (\bold{t}A,w;\bold{t}A',w')\colon\bold{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{r}, w,w'\in\mathbb{R}\Bigr\},
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
where $A$ and $A'$ are some full rank $r\times s$ matrices with height at most $F_{1}$. By Lemma \ref{dege}, we have that
\begin{equation}\nonumber
 \begin{split}
  [H_{i+1},H_{i+1}]=\Bigl\{ (\bold{0},\bold{s}AB^{G}A^{T}\bold{t}^{T};\bold{0},\bold{s}A'B^{G}A'^{T}\bold{t}^{T})\colon\bold{s},\bold{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{r}\Bigr\}.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
So we deduce that
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
  AB^{G}A^{T}=A'B^{G}A'^{T}.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}

If $rank(A)<s$, similar to the previous case, there exist $F_{3}>0$ and $\bold{p}=(\bold{p}_{0},\bold{0})\in\mathbb{Z}^{s}\times\{0\}^{s+2}$ with $0<\Vert\bold{p}\Vert\leq F_{3}$ such that
$\Vert\bold{p}\cdot\tilde{\bold{c}_{i+1}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}=\Vert\bold{p}_{0}\cdot\widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\leq\frac{F_{3}}{N}$.
Since the coefficients of each pair $(h_{j},h_{j+1}) (0\leq j\leq i)$ satisfy Property 2) of Lemma \ref{appro2} and $\bold{p}$ is of type 1 (and thus is of the same type
as all subgroups of $H_{0}$), there exists
$w\in\mathbb{Z}$ with $0<\vert w\vert\leq F_{4}$ such that
$\Vert w\bold{p}\cdot\tilde{\bold{c}_{0}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}=\Vert w\bold{p}_{0}\cdot\widehat{\bold{a}_{0}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\leq\frac{F_{4}}{N}$,
where $F_{4}=D'_{1}(F_{1}\cdot D'_{2}(\dots F_{1}\cdot D'_{i}(0)\dots))$. So the existence of $\eta_{1}$ in (i) is proved.
The existence of $\eta_{2}$ in (i) holds similarly and therefore conclustion (i) holds.

Now we assume that $rank(A)=s$. In this case $r\geq s$. Suppose that $A'=Y\binom{I_{s\times s}}{0_{(r-s)\times s}}$ for some
invertible $r\times r$ matrix $Y$. Denote $A=Y\binom{A_{1}}{A_{2}}$, where $A_{1}$ and $A_{2}$ are respectively $s\times s$ and $(r-s)\times s$ matrices.
Then (\ref{ABA}) implies that
\begin{equation}\nonumber
 \begin{split}
  & A_{1}B^{G}A_{1}^{T}=B^{G};
  \\& A_{2}B^{G}(A_{1}^{T},A_{2}^{T})=0.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
Note that $A_{1}B^{G}A_{1}^{T}=B^{G}$ implies that $A_{1}^{T}\in\Lambda(B^{G})$. Since $rank(A)=s$, $A_{2}B^{G}(A_{1}^{T},A_{2}^{T})=0$ implies that $A_{2}B^{G}=0$. Let $A''$ be the upper left $s'\times s'$ block of the matrix $A_{1}^{T}$. Since $A_{1}^{T}\in\Lambda(B^{G})$, we deduce that $A''\in\Lambda(B_{0}^{G})$.

Suppose that $\widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}=\bold{t}A, \widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}=\bold{t}A'$ for some $\bold{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{r}$. Then
$\widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}=\bold{s}\binom{A_{1}}{A_{2}}, \widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}=\bold{s}\binom{I_{s\times s}}{0_{s\times (r-s)}}$, where $\bold{s}=\bold{t}Y$. Denote $\bold{s}=(\bold{s}_{1},\bold{s}_{2}), \bold{s}_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{s}, \bold{s}_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{r-s}$.
Then $\widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}=\bold{s}_{1}, \widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}=\bold{s}_{1}A_{1}+\bold{s}_{2}A_{2}=\widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}A_{1}+\bold{s}_{2}A_{2}$. So $\widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}B^{G}=\widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}A_{1}B^{G}$.
Thus
$\widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}B^{G}A_{1}^{T}=\widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}A_{1}B^{G}A_{1}^{T}= \widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}B^{G}$.
Suppose that $\bold{s}_{3}\in\mathbb{R}^{s'}$ is the vector consisting of the first $s'$ entries of $\bold{s}_{1}$. Then
considering the first $s'$ entries of $\widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}B^{G}A_{1}^{T}$ and $\widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}B^{G}$, we get that
$\bold{a}_{i+1}^{\bullet}B_{0}^{G}A''=\bold{b}_{i+1}^{\bullet}B_{0}^{G}$.
Since the coefficients of each pair $(h_{j},h_{j+1}) (0\leq j\leq i)$ satisfy Property 2) of Lemma \ref{appro2}, we
deduce that $\bold{a}^{\bullet}B_{0}^{G}A''$ is at most $\frac{F_{5}}{N}$-away from $\bold{b}^{\bullet}B_{0}^{G}$ for some $F_{3}>0$ depending only on $X$ and $\kappa$, and $A''\in\Lambda(B_{0}^{G})$ is of height at most $F_{5}$. Therefore, conclusion
(ii) holds.

Since the coefficients of each pair $(h_{j},h_{j+1}) (0\leq j\leq i)$ satisfy Property 2) of Lemma \ref{appro2} and $\bold{p}$ is of type 1 (and thus is of the same type
as all subgroups of $H_{0}$), there exists

where $F_{4}=D'_{1}(F_{1}\cdot D'_{2}(\dots F_{1}\cdot D'_{i}(0)\dots))$. So the existence of $\eta_{1}$ in (i) is proved.

nodes.name: rank(A) = s: A_1^T in Lambda(B^G) gives conclusion (ii)
nodes.statement:
Now we assume that $rank(A)=s$. In this case $r\geq s$. Suppose that $A'=Y\binom{I_{s\times s}}{0_{(r-s)\times s}}$ for some
invertible $r\times r$ matrix $Y$. Denote $A=Y\binom{A_{1}}{A_{2}}$, where $A_{1}$ and $A_{2}$ are respectively $s\times s$ and $(r-s)\times s$ matrices.
Then (\ref{ABA}) implies that
\begin{equation}\nonumber
 \begin{split}
  & A_{1}B^{G}A_{1}^{T}=B^{G};
  \\& A_{2}B^{G}(A_{1}^{T},A_{2}^{T})=0.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
Note that $A_{1}B^{G}A_{1}^{T}=B^{G}$ implies that $A_{1}^{T}\in\Lambda(B^{G})$. Since $rank(A)=s$, $A_{2}B^{G}(A_{1}^{T},A_{2}^{T})=0$ implies that $A_{2}B^{G}=0$. Let $A''$ be the upper left $s'\times s'$ block of the matrix $A_{1}^{T}$. Since $A_{1}^{T}\in\Lambda(B^{G})$, we deduce that $A''\in\Lambda(B_{0}^{G})$.

Suppose that $\widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}=\bold{t}A, \widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}=\bold{t}A'$ for some $\bold{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{r}$. Then
$\widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}=\bold{s}\binom{A_{1}}{A_{2}}, \widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}=\bold{s}\binom{I_{s\times s}}{0_{s\times (r-s)}}$, where $\bold{s}=\bold{t}Y$. Denote $\bold{s}=(\bold{s}_{1},\bold{s}_{2}), \bold{s}_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{s}, \bold{s}_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{r-s}$.
Then $\widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}=\bold{s}_{1}, \widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}=\bold{s}_{1}A_{1}+\bold{s}_{2}A_{2}=\widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}A_{1}+\bold{s}_{2}A_{2}$. So $\widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}B^{G}=\widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}A_{1}B^{G}$.
Thus
$\widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}B^{G}A_{1}^{T}=\widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}A_{1}B^{G}A_{1}^{T}= \widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}B^{G}$.
Suppose that $\bold{s}_{3}\in\mathbb{R}^{s'}$ is the vector consisting of the first $s'$ entries of $\bold{s}_{1}$. Then
considering the first $s'$ entries of $\widehat{\bold{a}_{i+1}}B^{G}A_{1}^{T}$ and $\widehat{\bold{b}_{i+1}}B^{G}$, we get that
$\bold{a}_{i+1}^{\bullet}B_{0}^{G}A''=\bold{b}_{i+1}^{\bullet}B_{0}^{G}$.
Since the coefficients of each pair $(h_{j},h_{j+1}) (0\leq j\leq i)$ satisfy Property 2) of Lemma \ref{appro2}, we
deduce that $\bold{a}^{\bullet}B_{0}^{G}A''$ is at most $\frac{F_{5}}{N}$-away from $\bold{b}^{\bullet}B_{0}^{G}$ for some $F_{3}>0$ depending only on $X$ and $\kappa$, and $A''\in\Lambda(B_{0}^{G})$ is of height at most $F_{5}$. Therefore, conclusion
(ii) holds.
